question: How many valiant men drew the sword in Israel and Judah as counted by Joab?
summary: 2 Samuel 24:9 gives the census totals as 800,000 for Israel and 500,000 for Judah. 1 Chronicles 21:5 gives the same census as 1,100,000 for Israel and 470,000 for Judah. Both Israel and Judah numbers disagree between the two reports.

reconcile.connective: Defenders close the gap by ledger: Chronicles' larger Israel total folds in the 300,000 standing army that Samuel set aside, while Samuel's larger Judah total adds a 30,000 frontier force Chronicles omitted.

discrepancy.connective: One gathered commentator declines the reconciliation outright, granting that the two totals cannot both be right and tracing the gap to scribal corruption in the numbers.

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871), on 1 Chronicles 21:5 and 2 Samuel 24:9
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: Row-surfaced harmonizer keyed to the exact passage: resolves the 300,000 Israel gap via the standing army not reckoned in Samuel and the 30,000 Judah gap via a frontier army omitted in Chronicles. Used as the textual anchor because Haley's verbatim coverage of this specific number pair could not be confirmed.

link.title: 2 Samuel 24:9 — Why do the numbers of men recorded in 2 Samuel 24:9 and in 1 Chronicles 21:5-6 disagree?
link.note: Verified live + on-topic: cites both verses and harmonizes via the standing-army (288,000+) inclusion in Chronicles and the 30,000 frontier force excluded from Chronicles' Judah count — 'Both calculations are correct according to the groups which were included and excluded from each report.'

excerpts.excerpt_text: It amounted to one million one hundred thousand men in Israel, capable of bearing arms, inclusive of the three hundred thousand military (Ch1 27:1-9), which, being already enlisted in the royal service, were not reckoned (Sa2 24:9), and to four hundred seventy thousand men in Judah, omitting thirty thousand which formed an army of observation stationed on the Philistine frontier (Sa2 6:1).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Single sentence that resolves BOTH numeric differences at once: the 300,000 standing army accounts for the 1,100,000 vs 800,000 Israel gap, the 30,000 frontier force for the 500,000 vs 470,000 Judah gap, and it names both source verses (Ch1 27 / Sa2 24:9 / Sa2 6:1). Strongest single reconcile; parity-capped to one on this discrepancy_first row.
excerpts.source_note_text: Joab gave the sum of the number of the children of Israel--It amounted to one million one hundred thousand men in Israel, capable of bearing arms, inclusive of the three hundred thousand military (Ch1 27:1-9), which, being already enlisted in the royal service, were not reckoned (Sa2 24:9), and to four hundred seventy thousand men in Judah, omitting thirty thousand which formed an army of observation stationed on the Philistine frontier (Sa2 6:1). So large a population at this early period, considering the limited extent of the country and comparing it with the earlier census (Num. 26:1-65), is a striking proof of the fulfilment of the promise (Gen 15:5).

excerpts.attribution: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
excerpts.excerpt_text: Neither of these sums is too great, but they cannot be both correct; and which is the true number is difficult to say. … To attempt to reconcile them in every part is lost labor; better at once acknowledge what cannot be successfully denied …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Rare case the spec endorses: a gathered note itself CONCEDES the contradiction. Clarke grants the two totals 'cannot be both correct,' calls reconciling them 'lost labor,' and elsewhere in the same note attributes the gap to scribal mistake/corruption. First span ends on a real source period; second span (non-adjacent, sense-preserving join) truncated before the continuation 'that although the original writers...' → ' …'. This makes the discrepancy pole filled with a verbatim excerpt, so no named skeptic is needed (and Paine does NOT press this exact pair — verified — nor does SAB/DiMattei have a dedicated numbers row).
excerpts.source_note_text: In Israel eight hundred thousand - the men of Judah were five hundred thousand - In the parallel place, Ch1 21:5, the sums are widely different: in Israel one million one hundred thousand, in Judah four hundred and seventy thousand. Neither of these sums is too great, but they cannot be both correct; and which is the true number is difficult to say. The former seems the most likely; but more corruptions have taken place in the numbers of the historical books of the Old Testament, than in any other part of the sacred records. To attempt to reconcile them in every part is lost labor; better at once acknowledge what cannot be successfully denied, that although the original writers of the Old Testament wrote under the influence of the Divine Spirit, yet we are not told that the same influence descended on all copiers of their words, so as absolutely to prevent them from making mistakes. They might mistake, and they did mistake; but a careful collation of the different historical books serves to correct all essential errors of the scribes. See the Dissertations of Dr. Kennicott mentioned at the conclusion of the preceding chapter.
